summary: Describes installing collections next to playbooks in a project's `collections/ansible_collections/` directory and the benefits: consistent versions for all users, portability, versioning with the playbooks, and isolation from global installs.
questions: Can I keep collections inside my project folder next to the playbook?
What directory layout do I need for playbook-adjacent collections?
Why would I install collections locally in the project instead of globally?
How do I make sure everyone on my team uses the same collection version?

answer_card.title: Install collections adjacent to playbooks
answer_card.answer_md:
Put collections under a `collections/ansible_collections/` directory beside your playbook:

```text
./
├── play.yml
├── collections/
│   └── ansible_collections/
│       └── my_namespace/
│           └── my_collection/
```

Benefits: every user of the project gets the same collection version, the project is self-contained and portable across environments, collections are versioned with your playbooks, and they are isolated from global installs used by other projects.
